children: Chicago Mercantile Exchange lean hog futures fell to contract lows on Wednesday, pressured by sliding cash hog prices and thin demand from meat-packers ahead of next week's Thanksgiving holiday, analysts said.
Packers are expected to work a short schedule next week, reducing the need for slaughter-ready hogs.

"You've got Thanksgiving week coming up, so there's only so many hogs you're going to be able to slaughter, and producers are losing money on every single hog that they sell. So the incentive on their part is to try to market them as early as possible. (But) on the part of the packer, they can only run so much production next week," said Altin Kalo, economist at Steiner Consulting Group.

On the CME, December lean hog futures (LHZ26) settled down 1.750 cents at 51.350 cents per pound after hitting a contract low at 51.225 cents. February lean hogs (LHG27) ended down 1.175 cents at 57.150 cents a pound after hitting a contract low at 56.500 cents.
The CME's Lean Hog Index (.IHX), a two-day weighted average of cash hog prices, was last quoted at 56.86 cents per pound, its lowest value since August 2020.

Wholesale pork prices bounced from near six-year lows set a day earlier. The US Department of Agriculture priced pork carcasses on Wednesday afternoon at $69.48 per hundredweight, up $1.04 from $68.44 on Tuesday.
But weak consumer demand remained a headwind for the market.
"Product is not moving as well as people were hoping or expecting," Kalo said, adding that consumer demand for pork has been lagging behind beef and chicken.
CME cattle futures bounced as market players waited for cash cattle trade to develop and adjusted positions ahead of monthly feedlot data due from the USDA on Friday.

Ahead of Friday's USDA Cattle on Feed report, Reuters-surveyed analysts expect the government to report the number of US cattle in feedlots as of November 1 at 11.671 million head, or 99.7% of last year's total.
Analysts, on average, estimated October feedlot placements at 97% of year-earlier levels and October marketings at 94.9% of levels seen a year ago.
